Hi Jane —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and next steps from our security/compliance discovery: 

Call highlights:
- You confirmed Acme will be the data controller for the customer records we process on your behalf.
- Main concerns: DPA terms, SCC module selection for controller->processor flows, subprocessor disclosure, and data retention for EU users.
- You requested SOC 2 status and whether we can sign the DPA with a controller/processor alignment.

What I attached: 1) Redwood DPA draft (baseline we use for most SaaS customers) and 2) an SCC module matrix that shows the common choices for controller/processor relationships.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Acme would like to proceed under the controller-to-processor SCC (we typically use the controller->processor module when the customer is the controller and Redwood is the processor).
2) If you have any required DPA redlines, please mark them in the attached DPA and share with contracts@acme.com — happy to jump on a quick call with legal.
3) Confirm any specific subprocessor questions (we will provide the current subprocessor list and our subprocessor flow).

Quick answers to the things you asked on the call:
- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified (report available upon NDA).
- HIPAA: We can sign a BAA for covered use cases — let us know if PHI will be processed.
- Vendor questionnaire: We can either complete Acme's vendor questionnaire or share our security pack; if you prefer, I can send a OneTrust link to speed up the intake.

Proposed timeline: get SCC module confirmed this week -> finalize DPA redlines next week -> target DocuSign execution within two weeks (if legal cadence allows).

I looped Rishi from our legal/ops team on this thread to help with the DPA and SCC specifics. Let me know what works for you.

Thanks —
Marissa
